title: Attached pronoun table and practice sheet
subject: Arabic
source: Written for arabic/y8 lesson 18 (Attached pronoun table and practice sheet (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 18: My, your, his, her, our: possessive endings. Read the Arabic aloud, then do the tasks. Write in Arabic with all the harakat.

parts.text: ة opens into ت before an ending: أُسْرَت

panels.title: In sentences
points: أُسْرَتُنَا كَبِيرَةٌ: our family is big
أَخُوهُ طَوِيلٌ: his brother is tall
أُمُّهَا مُعَلِّمَةٌ: her mother is a teacher

head: Not this
This
rows: بَيْتِي: never use al- and a possessive ending together

questions.q: Core: Add the ending: 1) قَلَم + my 2) سَيَّارَة + our 3) غُرْفَة + her 4) كِتَاب + his 5) أُسْرَة + your (m).
Extend: Write four sentences about your family using our, his and her: e.g. بَيْتُنَا فِي ...
questions.a: For example: بَيْتُنَا فِي لَنْدَنَ. أُخْتِي طَالِبَةٌ وَمَدْرَسَتُهَا قَرِيبَةٌ. أَبِي مُهَنْدِسٌ وَسَيَّارَتُهُ بَيْضَاءُ.

questions.q: Stretch: Translate: Our grandmother lives with us, and her room is big.

questions.a: B) بَيْتُهَا. ـهَا means her; ـهُ means his.

questions.q: What does ـُنَا mean? A) our B) your C) his
Big question: how does one ending show who something belongs to? Give two examples.
questions.a: The attached pronoun shows the owner: بَيْتِي (my house), بَيْتُهَا (her house).
